grupos.claim: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, importers alias it as `BackupCode`, and the body renders the backup-code field, not the TOTP input.
grupos.evidence: apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:7 `export default function TwoFactor({ center = true }) {`; body renders backup_code label/instructions and TextField id="backup-code" registered as "backupCode"; importers apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:32 and apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8 both `import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode";`.

grupos.claim: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` at apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:53 can never fail; EnableTwoFactorModal.handleEnable sets step to DisplayBackupCodes instead of calling onEnable(), so the switch is unchecked until the user closes the backup-codes modal, which this test never does.

The page /settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:43-50 binds the switch to user?.twoFactorEnabled, invalidated only via onEnable.
grupos.reason: All facts the comment relies on hold: the assertion compares a Promise with toBeTruthy (always truthy, as the in-file FIXME admits), the settings modal's handleEnable only moves to DisplayBackupCodes, and the enable test never closes that modal.

grupos.claim: It only asserts a success toast is shown, but the component fires `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting it and shows the toast unconditionally afterwards.

grupos.claim: The generated backup codes are lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in setup.ts), but this validator matches the user input case-sensitively via `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`. The same case-sensitive comparison exists in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts.
grupos.evidence: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:61 `const backupCodes = Array.from(Array(10), () => crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"));` (lowercase hex producer); packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:144 `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));` (case-sensitive, no toLowerCase); apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:61 `const index = backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""));` (same case-sensitive comparison). grupos.claim: On a successful 2FA enable the modal advances to the backup-codes step (setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)) instead of calling onEnable(); onEnable() is only reachable through the 'Close' button, so dismissing the dialog via Escape/onOpenChange never calls onEnable() or resetState(), skipping the parent's utils.viewer.me.invalidate() and leaving the two-factor-switch disabled with stale step state.
grupos.evidence: apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:134-137 (setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); return;), :263-272 (only onEnable() call, in the Close button), :166 (onOpenChange passed through) with apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64-68 (onOpenChange only toggles; onEnable runs utils.viewer.me.invalidate()) and :37,43-45 (disabled={canSetupTwoFactor}, canSetupTwoFactor = !isCalProvider && !user?.twoFactorEnabled)
grupos.reason: Every fact the comment relies on checks out: the success path sets the backup-codes step, onEnable is invoked solely by the Close button, and neither onOpenChange nor resetState runs on Escape/overlay dismissal, so the parent's invalidate is skipped and the switch remains disabled with stale step state.

grupos.claim: Backup-code consumption at packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131-156 is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt, indexOf, null out, re-encrypt, update), so concurrent logins with the same single-use code can both persist it as consumed.
grupos.evidence: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-156 decrypts user.backupCodes, does indexOf (144), sets backupCodes[index]=null (148), and calls prisma.user.update unconditionally by id (149-156), with the user read at line 73; apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:2015 documents "Each backup code can be used exactly once".
grupos.reason: The cited code is exactly the non-atomic read-modify-write described and the single-use documentation exists, so the reported issue's factual basis holds.
